summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis and J-tube placement was readmitted one day after discharge due to a recurrent flare of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She was unable to tolerate oral intake or tube feeds initially. In the ED, she received IV fluids, lorazepam, and morphine, with improvement in symptoms. Admission labs showed mild hypokalemia and metabolic acidosis, both of which resolved with hydration. A contrast study confirmed proper J-tube placement without complications. Over the hospital stay, she gradually tolerated advancing tube feeds, discontinued IV medications, and resumed oral medications via the tube. Given her recent frequent hospitalizations, she was discharged with crushed lorazepam and morphine tablets to administer through her J-tube during future flares, along with follow-up appointments. She was ambulatory and stable at discharge.
